audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why called Level 1 "your worst level in the game" on a stage the chart correctly gives to Dr. Mundo, and phases[1].why opened "Still Akali's window" after a stage Mundo won. Every phase reason was shared template copy carrying no Akali-specific content.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw reaches 975 against Five Point Strike's 550 and costs Akali-relative nothing, while her Q costs 110 energy at rank 1 — Mundo wins the early chip war outright. The lane inverts at 3 when Twilight Shroud and Shuriken Flip come online, and inverts back once Mundo has two health items. Mirror (akali__drmundo) states the same range and energy facts from her side.
audit.corrected: Phase reasons rewritten around Bonesaw's 975 range, her 110 energy cost, Twilight Shroud's targeting rule and Maximum Dosage vs Perfect Execution.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: "level chart contradicts data: Dr. Mundo wins 52.95% but the chart gives Akali 5/7 stages vs 2". content win[6] and full phases[6].side both handed 2+ items to Akali, and win[4]/phases[4].side handed Level 6 to Dr. Mundo while whys[4] said "clearly Akali at 6".
audit.why: Akali's spikes are single-target burst; Mundo's spike is stacked health plus MR, which the burst cannot scale into. The mirror audit already records that Akali's page states "his health stacking outgrows single-target burst" at 2+ items, so 2+ items MUST be Dr. Mundo on both pages. Level 6 is genuinely even: Perfect Execution is a kill threat, but Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of missing health, which is exactly the resource her execute is measured against.
audit.corrected: Level 6 becomes Skill 5/10; 2+ items becomes Dr. Mundo 7/10; Level 2 rating raised to 5/10 to match its Skill token. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED ABILITY: five separate fields describe Dr. Mundo having an "E stun" — whys[4] "clearing your E stun", spikes[1].text "leap over your E stun angle", mid "dodge your E stun", late "her dashes clear your E angle", wants.you[1] "Land E (Blunt Force Trauma) stun". Blunt Force Trauma is an auto-attack reset with missing-health damage that swats away enemies it kills. Dr. Mundo has no stun anywhere in his kit; his only crowd control is the Infected Bonesaw slow. Separately, phases[2].why claimed "your passive shrugs the first CC" — Akali brings no immobilising effect, so Goes Where He Pleases never triggers in this lane, and the decisive targeting interaction was absent everywhere.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud (20/19/18/17/16s) makes Akali 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks'. Auto-attacks and Blunt Force Trauma both need to select her, so both are dead inside the smoke — but Infected Bonesaw is a skillshot that damages 'the first enemy hit', selecting nothing, so it still lands in the shroud, as does Heart Zapper's area burst if she is inside 325. That is the whole matchup: you fight the smoke with Q and W, never with autos or E. Perfect Execution (120/90/60s) is her kill button; Maximum Dosage (flat 120s) instantly heals a percent of missing health, so pressing it before her recast lifts you back off the execute. Assassin's Mark rings you on spell damage and empowers her next attack only when she exits the ring — stepping toward her denies the proc, and the auto wind-up, not the cast, is the tell.
audit.corrected: Twilight Shroud (20/19/18/17/16s) blocks autos and your E, not Infected Bonesaw — skillshots still land in the smoke.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twilight Shroud was quoted as a flat "(18s)" in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t. Riot's per-rank cooldown is 20/19/18/17/16 — 18s is rank 3. Shuriken Flip, her only gap-closer, was never given a number.
audit.why: Shuriken Flip is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. Once it is spent she has no way to reach you and no way to leave, which is the actual step-up window.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 numbers used and Shuriken Flip added to breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: tradeGood in this matchup is clean (no PDF scrape artifact, unlike the Aatrox entry) and the auto-into-E-reset sequence is accurate. Left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull and dontsFull are shared template copy with no Akali content, and dontsFull[2] tells you to save "your escape" — Dr. Mundo has no escape.
audit.why: His defensive tool is Maximum Dosage's heal, and the mistake worth naming is spending it on chip poke instead of holding it for the Perfect Execution recast.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to Twilight Shroud timing, the targeting rule and holding R for her recast.

notes: BIGGEST FIND: a fabricated Dr. Mundo ability. Five fields (whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid, late, wants.you[1]) told the player to land or protect an "E stun". Blunt Force Trauma has no stun — it is an auto-attack reset dealing missing-health damage that swats away enemies it kills. Dr. Mundo's only CC is the Infected Bonesaw slow. All five are corrected. Also removed the non-interaction in phases[2].why ("your passive shrugs the first CC") — Akali has no immobilising effect, so Goes Where He Pleases never fires in this lane; per the relevance rule I wrote nothing in its place about the passive at all. The packet's own defect (chart contradicts the 52.95% win rate) is fixed as an atomic group: Level 6 to Skill, 2+ items to Dr. Mundo. 2+ items had to flip regardless — the already-written mirror audit records Akali's page saying his health stacking outgrows her single-target burst, and the two pages cannot disagree. The Twilight Shroud targeting rule (autos and E are dead, Bonesaw and Heart Zapper are not) is the decisive interaction and was absent from every field; the mirror rated it Medium confidence, but Riot's own wording — 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks' versus Bonesaw's 'first enemy hit' — makes it High. Twilight Shroud was quoted as a flat 18s; real value is 20/19/18/17/16.
